items.title: James "Sing" Miller Interview, 1964-12-11
items.q: So I started up with some boys, four fellas, they're still living. Eddie Hickman, Julius Simpson, and a saxophone player... And we started there.

ctx.x: The End This is an interview with Mr. Singh Miller. This is Bill Russell doing the interviewing. And the date is about the tenth of... Is this the eleventh? Lost track of the date. The eleventh of December, 1964. We're recording this down at 732 St. Peter Street. What is your full name? My name is James Edward Miller. James Edward Miller. Everyone calls me Singh. How did you get that nickname? I've been singing since I was a little bit of a boy. Actually, from your singing? From school days. Now, where were you…

Can you remember some of the other bands you've worked with? You told about that first band that you played, the one on Dryad Street. I worked with Paul Barber, I worked with George Lewis, I worked with George Williams, I worked with the average band around here. Yeah, I guess you worked with a whole bunch of them. Yeah, around here. Like most of the musicians. I worked with Kit Howard, Sheik, Thomas, you know I work with Thomas now. I work with Thomas now. But I worked with Peter Burkhardt, I worked with Willie…

items.title: James "Sing" Miller Interview, 1971-01-17
items.q: I know Julius Simpson played drum, I know. Tony played trumpet.

ctx.x: All right, and who else played?
John Bruce, Julius Simpson, Buddy Charles. And way around 1940 when I met Cheek at the Cotton Club.
Mm-hmm. And this first job, was it a dance or?
